title: Reducing Keys in 2-TEM and 4-TEM
summary: The source reports no key-count reduction for either construction, and it remains open whether fewer independent keys can preserve security.

formal_statement.body: For the 2-TEM and 4-TEM tweakable Even-Mansour constructions, where 2-TEM uses two independent hash keys and 4-TEM uses two independent $n$-bit keys, determine whether the number of independent keys in either construction can be reduced while preserving its security. The unresolved task is to give such reduced-key constructions, or to establish that no such reduction is possible without degrading security.

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptographic design focused on tweakable Even-Mansour block-cipher constructions.
parameters: 2-TEM: two independent hash keys, whose count is the reduction target
4-TEM: two independent n-bit keys, whose count is the reduction target
scope.unresolved_remainder: Provide a reduced-key version of either construction that preserves security, or establish that no such reduction is possible without degrading security.

citations.label: Minimizing the Two-Round Tweakable Even-Mansour Cipher

progress.summary: The authors state that their 2-TEM construction requires two independent hash keys and their 4-TEM construction requires two independent n-bit keys. They present reducing the number of keys without degrading security as a natural open problem.
citation_labels: Avijit Dutta et al., Minimizing the Two-Round Tweakable Even-Mansour Cipher
